primitives.note: Resonance builds up to 3 stacks from basic attacks and damaging abilities, refreshing on hit; the 3rd stack consumes all stacks for bonus magic damage.
P's 3rd-stack bonus magic damage and W's missing-health bonus magic damage both ride on basic attacks.
W's on-hit damage magnitude is 3% (+3%/100AP) of the target's missing health.
W's on-hit damage only triggers while the target is below 30% max health.
Q's outgoing hit and R's arrival explosion are damage instances applied on cast/after a fixed delay.
Q deals a separate outgoing instance and a separate return instance, each hitting once.
The return-damage instance depends on the grenade travelling out, expanding, and homing back onto the same target; a dummy fight must assume this reliably connects.
E arms Ekko's next basic attack with bonus magic damage and a blink.
E's dash resets Ekko's basic attack timer, letting the empowered attack come out early.
R has a 0.5s (wiki) cast/stasis window before the dash and explosion resolve, delaying when its damage and heal land.
W's detonation shield (self, positional) and R's self-heal only matter to damage taken/survival, not to damage dealt.

needsBespoke.why: Every mechanic that matters to the damage/survival fight maps onto existing primitives: Resonance is target-stacks feeding an onhit-rider, W's passive is a threshold-gated conditional onhit-rider, Q is a two-part plain-cast whose return instance needs a positional assumption, E is an empowered-attack that also triggers attack-reset, and R is a charge-or-channel plain-cast plus a defensive-only heal. No kit-specific logic beyond combining these primitives is required.

proposal: Open by basic-attacking the dummy immediately to start building Resonance stacks.
Cast Q (Timewinder) on cooldown for its outgoing and later return magic-damage instances.
Weave E (Phase Dive) in right after a basic attack so its attack-reset lets the empowered, bonus-damage auto come out as early as possible; recast on cooldown.

Continue basic-attacking between ability casts so every 3rd hit consumes Resonance for its bonus magic damage, and so W's passive on-hit damage fires automatically once the dummy's health drops below 30%.
Cast R (Chronobreak) on cooldown purely for its own large magic-damage explosion; do not rely on its heal or stasis for anything in the damage fight.

Do not actively cast W for damage purposes, since its active only grants a self-shield/stun setup and deals no direct damage to a stationary, non-chasing dummy; let its passive on-hit component fire on its own.
Repeat: auto-attack + Q/E/R on cooldown, prioritizing not clipping auto-attacks, until the 15s window ends or the dummy dies.

Is it ever damage-optimal to cast W just to threaten/soften up (e.g., forcing the passive missing-health proc timing), or is it strictly correct to never actively cast W in the pure damage-race scenario?
